result:
Parking the roadmap: its one unticked stage and the three Ranked-list items go to the deferred backlog, and the roadmap retires as **PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete**. This also drops my earlier question about promoting O2.

I need to read three files before I write anything:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md   # Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                         # may not exist yet
Bash: ls specs/completed/
```

**1. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`** under `## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06`. There will be one item each, in the schema's format. Each item stands on its own, without the roadmap.

| Item | Size | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Stage 2 — closure notices (O5): email boat operators within an hour of a lock closing, from the closure log's live feed | small: one closure-log poll every 10 minutes | the notice job and its mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every listed address within an hour of a new closure entry |
| O2 — 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock from the river-level forecast | small: one model run a day, on Stage 1's fit (22 min on a laptop) | a daily 7-day closure-risk outlook exists for each lock |
| O3 — separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks | about 14 × Stage 1's data (roughly 25 GB). Fit time is unknown, because a pooled fit does not scale linearly from the 22-minute single fit | a closure curve exists for each of the 14 locks, fit jointly |
| O4 — closure-history map for boat operators | about a day: one static map page | operators can open a map of the closure history |

The O2, O3 and O4 items will each cite the result in `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`: the closure chance rises steeply above 3.1 m, and the four longest-record locks show nearly the same curve. Any future work starts from that result.

Stage 2's text-message notices are not parked. The roadmap never assigned them to a stage or a list item.

**2. Retire the roadmap.**

```
Edit specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md   # add under the title: PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete
Bash: mkdir -p specs/completed && git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/
```

There is no spec, methodology file or critique file to retire with it. The Stage 1 findings file stays in `specs/`, where the deferred items cite it.

**3. Commit on `main`.**

```
Bash: git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md && \
      git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (funding ended): 1 of 2 stages complete; remaining work to deferred_items"
```

Once these run, nothing is left to hand off: this roadmap is closed. If the funding comes back, the four items will be in `specs/deferred_items.md`, where /deferred picks them up.
